title: Romanticism in Literature and Art
text: Romanticism was an artistic, literary, musical, and intellectual movement that originated in Europe toward the end of the 18th century. It was partly a reaction against the rationalism of the Enlightenment and emphasized emotion, imagination, nature, and individualism. Literary Romantics include William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge (Lyrical Ballads, 1798), Lord Byron, Percy Bysshe Shelley, and John Keats in England; Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in Germany; and Victor Hugo and Alexandre Dumas in France. In visual art, Romanticism is represented by the works of Caspar David Friedrich, J.M.W. Turner, and Eugène Delacroix. American Romantics include Edgar Allan Poe and Herman Melville.
